title: Stream oscillation mitigation and function-call coordination for SSE streaming
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Implement an SSE streaming behavior that reduces client-server oscillation (frequent reconnects and duplicate fragments) while preserving strict function/tool-call atomicity and structured-output invariants. This ticket covers protocol-level framing, resume token semantics, and server-side heuristics to avoid repeated partial toolcall replays when clients reconnect. Scope: server runtime changes (framing, resume token lifetimes, fragment self-describing headers), client-backoff handshake hints, and compatibility shim for older clients that expect JSONL boundaries or idempotent chunk ids.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Server emits chunk metadata headers per SSE event: fragment_id, seq_in_fragment, toolcall_boundary, schema_hint.
2) Resume token contains last-accepted-fragment-id and last-emitted-kv-cache-offset and can be used to avoid re-sending completed toolcall frames.
3) On reconnect clients can provide resume token; server will not re-emit already-acknowledged toolcall frames and will stream a short 'resync' envelope indicating missing semantic gaps.
4) Function/tool-call outputs remain atomic: no partial toolcall payloads are considered final by default.
5) Backoff/oscillation heuristics reduce reconnect frequency by at least 60% for noisy mobile clients in internal perf tests.
6) Compatibility shim redirects legacy JSONL-boundary clients to a stable framing mode with sequence markers.
7) End-to-end tests and a canary rollout exist, with monitoring dashboards showing dropped reconnects and toolcall duplication rates before/after deployment.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions: 1) Use a hybrid resume token (opaque string) that encodes: last_fragment_id, fragment_length, kv_cache_offset, server_epoch. This keeps server-only state minimal and supports transparent migration. 2) Introduce 'toolcall_boundary' boolean in fragment headers; server will mark fragments that complete a function/tool call. Clients must treat fragments marked with completion as idempotent commit points. 3) To prevent oscillation, implement 'grace window' (500ms to 3s configurable) during which server will buffer a reconnect from same client token and reconcile before re-emitting fragments. 4) For structured-output compatibility, add schema_hint (e.g., json-schema id or 'jsonl' token) and allow the client to request strict or lenient framing. 5) Fallback: if client doesn't support resume tokens, server will fall back to last-good-snapshot re-send but will attach 'probable-duplicate' markers to toolcall envelopes for consumer de-dup logic. 6) Metrics: emit counters for reconnect_count, duplicate_toolcall_emitted, fragments_replayed, resume_token_rejected.
Trade-offs: the grace window reduces immediate availability for new connections from same token; kept short to minimize impact. Resume tokens eat a small amount of metadata but avoid heavier per-session storage.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token encoding/decoding, fragment header parsing, and toolcall boundary marking. Integration tests: simulate intermittent network (random drops) across a range of latencies and packet loss; assert no duplicate completed toolcall payloads delivered to function router. Load test: 10k concurrent streams with mixed mobile/desktop reconnection patterns to verify oscillation metrics. Canary plan: 1% of traffic runtime-1.20, monitor duplicate_toolcall_emitted and reconnect_count for 48 hours, promote if <10% change in latency P95 and duplicate_toolcall_emitted reduced. Manual QA will validate compatibility shim by running legacy JS client against canary and verifying JSONL consumers still parse frames correctly.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy server-side framing and resume token support behind feature-flag (runtime-1.20.ff_stream_resume). 2) Expose a client-backoff hint header in API responses (X-Stream-Backoff: suggested-ms). 3) Roll canary to 1% traffic for 48h with detailed dashboards. 4) If metrics good, progress to 10% then 50% over a week. 5) During rollout, enable 'compatibility-mode' for customers who opt-out via tenancy flag to avoid breaking older SDKs. 6) Post-rollout: deprecate older JSONL-only stream modes after 60 days with customer notifications.
